name: Sheldon Whitehouse
groups: Ranking Member, Senate Committee on Environment and Public Works
signature: Author of the Clean Cloud Act to make AI data centers pay for dirty power; leads the Senate push to repeal Section 230.

notable_quote.text: we don't have to choose between leading the world on AI and leading the world on climate safety: big technology and AI companies have all the money in the world to pay for developing new sources of clean energy

data_centers.summary: Whitehouse is the Senate's leading voice for making AI data centers pay their own way. He wrote the Clean Cloud Act to charge big data centers for dirty power, led letters to protect New England electric customers, and is pressing EPA to act on xAI's unpermitted gas turbines. He says the U.S. can lead on AI and climate at the same time, and he was open to a permitting deal to speed grid upgrades.

evidence.title: S.1475 Clean Cloud Act of 2025 (sponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: His own bill would have EPA set an emissions standard for data centers and crypto mines and charge them a rising fee when their power is too dirty, with a quarter of the money going to low-income ratepayers.

evidence.title: Press release: Whitehouse, Fetterman introduce Clean Cloud Act
evidence.quote: Energy-hungry data centers and cryptomining facilities are overloading our already strained power grid, driving up consumers' electricity costs, making it harder for Americans to power their homes and businesses, and spiking fossil fuel emissions
evidence.what_it_shows: In his own words he blames data centers for higher electric bills and more pollution, and wants tech companies to pay for new clean power.

evidence.title: Letter: Reed and Whitehouse lead six New England senators asking ISO New England how it will protect ratepayers from data center costs
evidence.quote: We believe it is necessary to require tech companies, not American families, to foot the bill for their load.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants the grid operator to make data center owners, not households, pay for the power demand they add.

evidence.title: Letter: Whitehouse and colleagues urge Biden White House to reconsider fast-tracking AI data centers
evidence.quote: we urge you to uphold critical clean air and water standards and ensure that the energy needs of technology companies are not prioritized over the needs of households
evidence.what_it_shows: Even under a Democratic president he opposed speeding up data center construction if it meant weaker pollution rules or higher household bills.

evidence.title: Letter: Whitehouse, Heinrich and Van Hollen probe nine companies over gas-powered AI data centers (Latitude Media)
evidence.quote: Gas turbines are not the only option for data center developers looking to meet booming demand
evidence.what_it_shows: He is investigating Meta, OpenAI, xAI and others over plans to run AI data centers on gas plants, pushing them toward cleaner power.

evidence.title: Letter: Whitehouse asks EPA to take enforcement action against xAI's Memphis-area data center (E&E News)
evidence.quote: xAI's strategy of installing turbines first and seeking permits after the fact is clearly illegal
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants federal regulators to crack down on an AI company that ran gas turbines without air permits.

evidence.title: S.Res.564 recognizing that solar, storage and wind can quickly and cheaply meet U.S. power demand growth (sponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: His answer to rising AI power demand is renewables and batteries rather than new gas plants.

evidence.title: Politico: Whitehouse and Heinrich joint statement as Senate Democrats end permitting reform talks
evidence.quote: There was a deal to be had that would have taken politics out of permitting, made the process faster and more efficient, and streamlined grid infrastructure improvements nationwide
evidence.what_it_shows: He was willing to speed up permitting for grid projects, so he is not against building, but walked away after the administration attacked offshore wind.

ai_risk.summary: Whitehouse backs targeted AI rules: keeping kids away from AI companion chatbots, banning AI fakes that trick voters, and bias testing for automated decision systems. No statement was found calling advanced AI an existential danger or seeking licensing or a pause.

evidence.title: S.3062 GUARD Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports requiring AI chatbot companies to verify ages and keep minors away from AI companion bots.

evidence.title: Roll Call: Senate Judiciary advances GUARD Act; Whitehouse ties kids' chatbot safety to repealing Section 230
evidence.what_it_shows: During the committee markup of the chatbot bill he argued Congress should also protect kids on other online platforms by repealing the Section 230 liability shield.

evidence.title: S.4774 Fraudulent Artificial Intelligence Regulations (FAIR) Elections Act of 2026 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports rules against using AI-made fake video and audio to deceive voters.

evidence.title: S.2892 Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2023 (cosponsor, 118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed making big companies test automated decision systems for bias and harm and report results to the FTC.

evidence.title: S.2325 Algorithmic Justice and Online Platform Transparency Act (cosponsor, 118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed transparency rules for the algorithms that pick what people see online and a ban on discriminatory algorithms.

tech_regulation.summary: Whitehouse wants to rein in Big Tech. He is a lead cosponsor of the bipartisan bill to repeal Section 230, backs tougher antitrust law against giant mergers, and supports the Kids Online Safety Act and the EARN IT Act.

evidence.title: S.3546 Sunset Section 230 Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports ending the law that shields online platforms from lawsuits over user content.

evidence.title: Uprise RI: Whitehouse announces he is filing a bipartisan Section 230 repeal with Sen. Graham
evidence.quote: At long last, we are proceeding to file a bipartisan Section 230 repeal
evidence.what_it_shows: In his own words he has pushed for years to strip platforms of their legal immunity.

evidence.title: S.130 Competition and Antitrust Law Enforcement Reform Act of 2025 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports making it harder for giant companies, including Big Tech, to merge.

evidence.title: S.1748 Kids Online Safety Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a duty of care requiring apps and platforms to protect minors.

evidence.title: S.1207 EARN IT Act of 2023 (cosponsor, 118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed removing platforms' legal shield when they allow child sexual abuse material to spread.

evidence.title: S.1094 Journalism Competition and Preservation Act of 2023 (cosponsor, 118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed letting news outlets bargain together to make Google and Facebook pay for their stories.

preemption.summary: Whitehouse voted with 98 other senators to strip the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws from the 2025 budget bill, but no statement, letter or bill was found on federal preemption of state AI laws, the December 2025 executive order, or the March 2026 White House framework as of Sept 2026.

evidence.title: Senate roll call 363: Yea on Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year state AI law moratorium from H.R.1 (99-1)
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined the near-unanimous vote to remove the moratorium, but almost every senator did, so the vote alone does not show a position.

china_chips.summary: No public position found on chip export controls or Nvidia sales to China as of Sept 2026. Searched his press releases and news for Nvidia, export controls and chips; he did not sign the Senate Democratic letters on H20 and H200 sales that Sen. Reed signed.

search_notes: Searches run: Google News for Whitehouse plus artificial intelligence; data centers; chatbot/deepfake; preemption/moratorium; Section 230; Judiciary AI hearings; Nvidia/export controls; Clean Cloud Act; ISO New England; AI regulation. Wayback URL listing of whitehouse.senate.gov with three keyword filters. Pages read: EPW Clean Cloud Act release, Reed/Whitehouse ISO-NE release and the letter PDF (dated Jan 23 2026), Dec 2024 data center executive order letter, E&E News xAI probe, Latitude Media gas data center probe, Roll Call GUARD Act markup, Uprise RI and The Hill on the Sunset Section 230 Act, Politico permitting talks, govtrack S.Res.564, Tech Policy Press Jan 2024 AI hearing transcript (his questions were neutral, not used). senate.gov and epw.senate.gov blocked direct fetch and the Wayback Machine was refusing connections, so those pages were read as raw page text through the r.jina.ai reader proxy; quotes were checked against that text. Nothing found on preemption or chip exports. Finbold reported he sold up to $500,000 of Nvidia stock in May 2026; not a policy position, omitted. The Providence Business News June 2026 Chamber breakfast article (AI discussion) is paywalled and could not be read.

name: Jack Reed
groups: Ranking Member, Senate Armed Services Committee
signature: Top Democrat on Armed Services; co-author of the Responsible AI in Defense Act and a steady critic of selling advanced Nvidia chips to China.

notable_quote.text: There was unanimous consensus that there should be federal regulation of AI and it should be done rapidly, but very carefully.

data_centers.summary: Reed led a letter from six New England senators asking the regional grid operator how it will keep AI data centers from raising household electric bills, saying the AI industry should pay those costs. He also wants the AI buildout to happen in America rather than the Middle East, so he is not against building data centers.

evidence.title: Letter: Reed and Whitehouse lead six New England senators asking ISO New England how it will protect ratepayers from data center costs
evidence.quote: As the ones who stand to benefit most, the multi-billion-dollar AI industry should be responsible for these costs.
evidence.what_it_shows: He wants tech companies, not families, to pay for the grid costs data centers create.

evidence.title: Joint statement of Reed, Coons, Shaheen, Warner, Kelly, Himes and Krishnamoorthi on Trump's UAE and Saudi AI chip deals
evidence.quote: Under this deal, data centers and AI systems that would otherwise be built in America will be built in the Middle East
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats data centers as valuable infrastructure that should be built in the U.S., which tempers his ratepayer concerns.

ai_risk.summary: Reed has said since 2023 that AI needs federal regulation done quickly but carefully. His main work is on military AI: he co-wrote a bill requiring human oversight and a manual override for AI weapons and barring AI from nuclear launch decisions, much of which the Senate Armed Services Committee folded into its 2027 defense bill. He also backed an office to check the most powerful AI models for serious dangers.

evidence.title: S.4707 Responsible Artificial Intelligence Defense Act of 2026 (cosponsor with Sen. Coons)
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill sets rules so the Pentagon keeps humans in the loop on AI weapons and bars AI from deciding to launch a nuclear weapon.

evidence.title: Axios: Coons and Reed to introduce the Responsible Artificial Intelligence in Defense Act
evidence.quote: A rigorous framework for human oversight is not a brake on adoption; it is the foundation that makes sustainable, confident adoption possible.
evidence.what_it_shows: The sponsors' memo frames binding human oversight rules as the way to adopt military AI safely, written after the Pentagon's fight with Anthropic.

evidence.title: Arms Control Association: Senate Armed Services Committee adopts AI and autonomous weapons framework based on the Coons-Reed bill in the FY2027 NDAA
evidence.what_it_shows: As ranking member he got most of his human-judgment and testing rules for military AI, including a ban on AI nuclear launch decisions, into the committee's defense bill.

evidence.title: Press release: Reed attends first Senate AI Insight Forum
evidence.quote: There was unanimous consensus that there should be federal regulation of AI and it should be done rapidly, but very carefully.
evidence.what_it_shows: In his own words he supports federal AI regulation and says there are dangers as well as benefits to sort out.

evidence.title: S.5616 Preserving American Dominance in Artificial Intelligence Act of 2024 (cosponsor, 118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed creating a government office to evaluate the most powerful AI models for serious dangers before release.

evidence.title: Letter: Reed, Brown, Menendez and Smith urge CFPB to act on AI voice-cloning scams
evidence.quote: The FTC and CFPB need to take action to help thwart this type of fraud
evidence.what_it_shows: Wants regulators to use existing powers against AI-enabled scams.

evidence.title: The Hill: Reed questions Pentagon CIO on labeling Anthropic a supply chain risk while still using Claude in the Iran war
evidence.what_it_shows: He pressed the Pentagon on why it punished an AI company that resisted broad military uses of its model, calling it odd that the department kept using the product.

tech_regulation.summary: Reed supports targeted online rules, chiefly the Kids Online Safety Act, the STOP CSAM Act, and letting news outlets bargain with Google and Facebook. He has not called for breaking up tech companies or repealing Section 230.

evidence.title: S.1748 Kids Online Safety Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a duty of care for platforms to protect minors.

evidence.title: Press release: Reed helps build momentum for bipartisan Kids Online Safety Act
evidence.quote: Ensuring a safe environment online should be the default, especially for children.
evidence.what_it_shows: In his own words he wants tech and social media companies held accountable for harm to kids.

evidence.title: S.1829 STOP CSAM Act of 2025 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports making platforms report and remove child sexual abuse material and letting victims sue.

evidence.title: S.1094 Journalism Competition and Preservation Act of 2023 (cosponsor, 118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed letting news outlets team up to make Google and Facebook pay for their stories.

preemption.summary: Reed voted with 98 other senators to strip the state AI law moratorium from the 2025 budget bill, but no statement, letter or bill was found on preempting state AI laws, the December 2025 executive order, or the March 2026 White House framework as of Sept 2026.

evidence.title: Senate roll call 363: Yea on Blackburn amendment striking the 10-year state AI law moratorium from H.R.1 (99-1)
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined the near-unanimous vote to remove the moratorium, but almost every senator did, so the vote alone does not show a position.

china_chips.summary: Reed is a consistent hawk on AI chip exports. He signed every major Senate Democratic letter against the Trump administration's H20 and H200 sales to China and its Gulf chip deals, and in his own words called the H200 decision a flawed, transactional move that could gift China's military key technology.

evidence.title: Press release: Reed and colleagues warn Trump's U-turn on AI chip sales to China is a colossal economic and national security failure
evidence.quote: This flawed, transactional decision without a broader AI export control strategy could gift China's military key technology gains and seems completely divorced from any consideration of America's economic and national security interests
evidence.what_it_shows: His own words opposing the December 2025 decision to let Nvidia sell H200 chips to China.

evidence.title: Joint statement of Reed, Coons, Shaheen, Warner, Kelly, Himes and Krishnamoorthi on Trump's UAE and Saudi AI chip deals
evidence.quote: AI chips must only be exported to trusted companies, in reasonable numbers, and in concert with credible security standards and assurances.
evidence.what_it_shows: He opposed exporting large volumes of advanced chips to the Gulf without security assurances against diversion to China.

evidence.title: Letter: Coons, Warner, Schumer, Reed and Warren to Commerce Secretary Lutnick on resuming Nvidia H20 sales to China
evidence.quote: We shouldn't be trading away key technological advantages as if they are concessions in a trade negotiation
evidence.what_it_shows: He objected to loosening chip export controls as part of trade talks with China.

evidence.title: Letter: Warner, Schumer, Reed, Shaheen, Coons and Warren to President Trump on the 15 percent fee deal for Nvidia and AMD chip sales to China
evidence.quote: We again urge your administration to quickly reverse course and abandon this reckless plan to trade away U.S. technology leadership.
evidence.what_it_shows: He asked Trump to reverse the deal letting Nvidia and AMD sell AI chips to China for a cut of revenue.

evidence.title: Letter: Schumer and Warren lead Senate Democrats including Reed urging Lutnick and Rubio to reconsider the Saudi and UAE chip deals
evidence.quote: These deals greenlight the sale of sensitive U.S. technology in exchange for illusory promises of foreign investment.
evidence.what_it_shows: He signed on to the argument that the Gulf deals risk sensitive chips reaching China.

search_notes: Searches run: Google News for Reed plus artificial intelligence; data centers; Nvidia/export controls/chips; NDAA AI; Anthropic/autonomous weapons; Kids Online Safety; electricity/ISO New England; AI super PACs and primary; preemption/moratorium. Wayback URL listing of reed.senate.gov with two keyword filters. Pages read: Reed Dec 2025 H200 release, ISO-NE release and letter PDF, House Intelligence Democrats joint statement on Gulf chip deals, Coons H20 letter release, Warner 15 percent fee letter release, Schumer/Warren Gulf letter release (all confirm Reed as signer), Reed AI Insight Forum release, CFPB voice-cloning letter release, Reed KOSA release, Axios on the Responsible AI in Defense Act, Arms Control Association on the SASC FY27 NDAA, The Hill on Reed questioning the Pentagon about Anthropic, NY Post on the Hegseth hearing. reed.senate.gov and other senate.gov pages blocked direct fetch and the Wayback Machine was refusing connections, so they were read as raw page text through the r.jina.ai reader proxy. Exact dates of the Coons and Warner letters were not shown in the proxy text, so month-level dates are given. Nothing found on preemption. Punchbowl and Politico Anthropic pieces were behind paywalls or rate limits. The Providence Business News June 2026 breakfast article is paywalled. No AI super PAC spending in his 2026 primary was found.

name: Gabe Amo
groups: Vice Ranking Member, House Foreign Affairs Committee
Ranking Member, House Science, Space, and Technology Subcommittee on Environment
signature: Co-lead of the bipartisan LIFT AI Act for K-12 AI literacy; challenged Trump's approval of Nvidia H200 chip sales to China.

notable_quote.text: AI is here, it's here to stay, and we need to prepare the next generation for this new reality

data_centers.summary: No statement on data centers was found as of Sept 2026. Amo cosponsored a Democratic energy bill that would make large users like data centers pay in full for the grid upgrades they cause, and he voted against the House Republican permitting bill. Both are weak, party-line signals.

evidence.title: H.R.7977 Energy Bills Relief Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: The 421-page Democratic bill includes a section on avoiding cost shifts onto families that makes large-load facilities such as data centers their own customer class that must fully pay for the grid upgrades they require.

evidence.title: House roll call 356: Nay on passage of H.R.4776, the SPEED Act permitting bill
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted against the Republican bill to speed environmental reviews for energy and other projects; nearly all Democrats did, so it is a weak signal.

ai_risk.summary: Amo's own AI work is about teaching students and small businesses to use AI, not restricting it. But he signed a 2026 letter calling AI a clear risk that demands hearings with AI CEOs under oath, has warned about AI misinformation, praised the AI Safety Institute, and cosponsored a ban on AI fakes that deceive voters.

evidence.title: Letter: Casar leads 20 House Democrats including Amo demanding Speaker Johnson hold hearings with AI CEOs under oath
evidence.quote: The CEOs of the largest AI companies should answer questions under oath, and Americans should have a chance to hear from independent experts on the dangers posed by this technology.
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined a letter saying AI poses a clear risk to safety and threatens millions of jobs, and that Congress has failed to respond.

evidence.title: American Bazaar: Amo on the Regulating AI podcast about AI literacy, misinformation and oversight
evidence.quote: This time is unique because of the speed with which information moves
evidence.what_it_shows: He called AI misinformation one of the biggest threats to democracy, said the AI Safety Institute was a bold step on mitigating risk, and wants oversight so AI platforms give accurate election information.

evidence.title: H.R.4894 Deceptive Practices and Voter Intimidation Prevention Act of 2025 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports making it illegal to spread lies about voting, including AI-made fakes, before federal elections.

evidence.title: Press release: Amo secures committee passage of the bipartisan LIFT AI Act for K-12 AI literacy
evidence.quote: AI is here, it's here to stay, and we need to prepare the next generation for this new reality
evidence.what_it_shows: His signature AI bill funds AI literacy for students and teachers, a pro-adoption approach endorsed by Google and OpenAI as well as teachers' unions.

evidence.title: H.R.5584 LIFT AI Act (co-lead with Rep. Kean; listed as cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: National Science Foundation grants for K-12 AI literacy curriculum and teacher training; neutral on AI risk.

tech_regulation.summary: No public position found on Section 230, antitrust, privacy law or kids online safety bills as of Sept 2026. Searched his press releases and news for Big Tech, Section 230, TikTok, privacy and kids online safety and found only an election-deception bill, which is counted under AI risk.

preemption.summary: Amo signed the November 2025 letter from 81 House Democrats opposing any revival of the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws in the defense bill and opposing the planned executive order to preempt state AI laws. No personal statement on preemption was found.

evidence.title: Letter: Matsui leads 81 House Democrats including Amo opposing an AI moratorium in the NDAA and a preemption executive order
evidence.quote: our strong opposition to any effort in the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) that would reintroduce a sweeping moratorium on the ability of states and local governments to enforce their own artificial intelligence (AI) laws and regulations
evidence.what_it_shows: He is on record against Congress or the White House blocking states from enforcing their own AI laws.

evidence.title: House roll call 145: Nay on House passage of H.R.1, which carried the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted against the House budget bill that contained the state AI law moratorium, but the bill covered many other issues, so this is a weak signal.

china_chips.summary: Amo is a chip export hawk. With Foreign Affairs Ranking Member Meeks he challenged the Trump administration's approval of Nvidia H200 sales to China as dangerous and likely illegal, he sponsored a bill to help small businesses comply with export controls, and he cosponsored bills to close the cloud-access loophole and put more export enforcement officers overseas.

evidence.title: Press release: Amo, Meeks challenge Trump and Secretary Lutnick's plan to sell advanced AI chips to China
evidence.quote: The United States must continue to ensure that we prevent China from accessing advanced AI chips to maintain our superior AI capabilities.
evidence.what_it_shows: His letter calls the H200 decision a threat to national security and says the 25 percent revenue share is likely illegal under export control law.

evidence.title: H.R.8288 Strengthening Export Controls Compliance Act (sponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: His own bill would help small businesses understand and follow rules on selling sensitive technology overseas.

evidence.title: H.R.2683 Remote Access Security Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports closing the loophole that lets foreign users reach restricted American chips and AI through the cloud.

evidence.title: H.R.4505 Export Controls Enforcement Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports stationing at least 20 export control officers overseas to catch chip smuggling.

Wayback URL listing of amo.house.gov with two filters, plus his live press release listing (pages 1 to 4) and his Committees and Caucuses page.
